transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, honestly, what finally made me make the appointment is this constant tightness I've been feeling. My neck, my shoulders, and even my jaw... they're just tight almost all the time now. It feels like I'm constantly bracing myself for some kind of bad news, even when I'm just sitting at my desk grading papers or trying to watch TV in the evening. It just won't let up.
About how long have you been experiencing this constant tension and feeling like you're bracing for bad news?
It's been about seven months now. I guess it really started back when a pipe burst at the house. The remodeling just threw the whole place into chaos, and... well, I've just felt this way ever since.
Aside from the issues with the house, do you find yourself worrying about a variety of other everyday matters, such as work or family?

Yeah, I do. It's like my mind just keeps jumping from one thing to the next. I'll be worrying about whether the contractors missed something with the house, and then right away I'm stressing about work—wondering if my lesson plans are slipping, or if the robotics kids are falling behind. And then it shifts to my family, and I start worrying that I'm disappointing my wife by not keeping everything under control. It just feels like I'm worrying about all of it, all the time.
When these worries start, do you find it difficult to stop or control them?

Yeah, I really do. It's... well, it's like I can't just turn it off. I can tell myself to stop, you know, try to just focus on the class right in front of me. But then one small thought pops in—maybe about a late invoice for the repairs, or a student who's falling behind—and it just sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. Once that starts, I just can't seem to shut it down.
How has all this worry and tension been affecting your sleep?

To be honest, I haven't really noticed it affecting my sleep too much. Um... I mean, once I actually get into bed and close my eyes, I seem to sleep okay. I'm not really sure if the worry is changing anything there. I just haven't really had any major issues with it, I guess.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating on your work, or does your mind ever seem to go blank?

No, not really. I mean, I can still focus on my lesson plans and teaching the kids just fine. I haven't had any moments where my mind just goes completely blank or anything like that. I'm pretty much able to get my work done like usual.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable or having a shorter temper than usual lately?

No, I wouldn't say so. I haven't really felt more irritable or anything. I mean, I still have the same patience with my students and my family. I don't think I've been snapping at anyone or losing my temper more than I normally would. So, no, that hasn't really been an issue for me.
Aside from the physical tension, do you often find yourself feeling restless, keyed up, or on edge?

Yes, I definitely feel that way. I'm pretty much wound up most of the day. It's like I'm just waiting for something else to go wrong. I even catch myself pacing around the classroom when the kids aren't there, or I'll be constantly checking my phone for messages from the contractor between periods. I just can't seem to settle down.
Do you find yourself feeling easily fatigued or tiring out more quickly than usual?

Yes, I do. Honestly, by the time the last bell rings, I feel completely wrung out. And it's... it's a kind of tired that a decent night's sleep or a quiet Sunday doesn't really fix. Even doing something routine, like sitting down to grade a short stack of quizzes, it just feels like I'm pushing through mud. I just don't have any energy left by the end of the day.
